key_insight: M3CoTBench provides a targeted benchmark to evaluate Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on medical image understanding, showing that CoT prompts reveal strengths and systematic gaps in stepwise clinical reasoning that are not captured by final-answer accuracy alone.
problem_solved: Existing medical image benchmarks focus on final answers and ignore intermediate diagnostic reasoning; there is no standard way to measure the quality, faithfulness, and clinical alignment of CoT outputs from MLLMs.
method: Curate medical image tasks (e.g., radiology, dermatology) with structured questions and expert-annotated CoT reasoning traces as ground truth.
Design evaluation protocol combining automated metrics (answer accuracy, step-level correctness, faithfulness, calibration) with expert human review for clinical alignment.
Benchmark multiple MLLMs and prompting strategies (CoT prompting vs direct-answer) and analyze failure modes, localization alignment, and reasoning depth.
impact: Provides practitioners a standardized way to measure and compare MLLM reasoning transparency and safety in clinical imaging, guiding model selection, prompt design, and targeted improvements for diagnostically reliable multimodal systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → CoT annotation → evaluation metrics → model comparison (shows workflow of M3CoTBench).
Side-by-side example: medical image with (a) final answer-only output vs (b) Chain-of-Thought output annotated by experts.
Bar chart: model performance across metrics (final accuracy, step-level correctness, faithfulness, calibration) to highlight trade-offs.
Heatmap/overlay: attention or localization alignment between model-highlighted image regions and expert-annotated salient areas.
paper_title: M3CoTBench: Benchmark Chain-of-Thought of MLLMs in Medical Image Understanding
paper_authors: Juntao Jiang, Jiangning Zhang, Yali Bi, Jinsheng Bai, Weixuan Liu
